cpu_sizing_decision.question: Should ClairS pileup_variants / evaluate_candidates use more than 4 CPU for the 150-pair production config?

pileup_variants.verdict: NOT CPU-bound. At the tuned 4-CPU allocation the process used only ~1 core (4-25% efficiency across the 4 completed shards). Adding CPUs does not help and wastes money. Right-size DOWN to 2 CPU for production. This directly answers the customer's 'can we use more than 4 CPU?' question with measured data: no.
pileup_variants.caveat: Only 4 pileup_variants shards completed before the operator cancelled the run; the straggler shard was in the evaluate_candidates (full-alignment) stage, not pileup. Efficiency signal is consistent across the 4 measured shards.

evaluate_candidates.note: No evaluate_candidates shard produced completion metrics: the run's single long-pole straggler (shard #341, taskId 9305854) was stuck at ClairS full-alignment on a pathological region with zero log progress for many hours even at the tuned 4-CPU allocation, and was cut by operator cancellation. The absence of progress at 4 CPU is itself the measurement.
evaluate_candidates.verdict: NOT a CPU-throughput problem. A single hard region that makes zero progress at 4 CPU will not be rescued by more cores per shard - ClairS full-alignment on one region is largely sequential. The correct production fix is FINER REGION SHARDING (split the pathological interval into smaller chunks so no single shard monopolises the critical path), NOT a larger per-shard cpus value. Recommend keeping cpus=4 (or even 2) and adding sub-region chunking for full-alignment.

companion_stages_that_DO_scale.sv_severus: omics.m.4xlarge, max CPU util 90.8% - genuinely thread-scaling; keep at 16 threads (already set). Flagged under-provisioned on peak.
companion_stages_that_DO_scale.note: minimap2 mapping and severus SV calling scale with threads and are already tuned to 16; the ClairS NN-inference processes (pileup_variants / evaluate_candidates) are the ones that do NOT scale.

top_over_provisioned_tasks.rationale: Memory efficiency ~11% - the m-family (4 GiB/CPU) is wasted; c-family (2 GiB/CPU) covers the ~1-2 GiB actual footprint. Largest single savings lever.
Single most expensive task. Peaks at 90.8% CPU so it IS thread-bound at peak; the m-family memory is over-allocated. c-family keeps the memory:CPU ratio tighter.
Most shards under 50% CPU efficiency at 8 CPU; smallest shards should drop to c.large / c.xlarge.
The tuned 4-CPU allocation is wasted (see cpu_sizing_decision.pileup_variants).

cancellation.reason: Operator cancelled after essentially the entire pipeline completed EXCEPT one straggler snv:evaluate_candidates shard (#341, taskId 9305854) hung at ClairS full-alignment on a pathological region with zero log progress for many hours even at 4 CPU. Root cause already understood - not a pipeline failure. DiagnoseAHORunFailure intentionally NOT run.
cancellation.not_a_duration_cap: Cancellation was manual, well within the 72h run-group cap (wall-clock ~8.5h).
